title: The largest of several
description:
Write `int max_of(int count, ...)` that returns the largest of `count` integers, and `double mean_of(int count, ...)` that returns the average of `count` doubles. Both return 0 when `count` is 0 or less.

```c
max_of(4, 3, 9, -2, 7)        /* 9 */
mean_of(3, 1.0, 2.0, 6.0)     /* 3.0 */
```
hints: Start the largest with the first argument, not with 0: all the numbers might be negative.
The doubles come out with `va_arg(args, double)`; a `float` argument has already been promoted to `double` on the way in.
unitTests:
TEST("max") { CHECK_EQ(max_of(4, 3, 9, -2, 7), 9); CHECK_EQ(max_of(1, -5), -5); CHECK_EQ(max_of(3, -9, -4, -7), -4); CHECK_EQ(max_of(0), 0); }
TEST("mean") { CHECK_NEAR(mean_of(3, 1.0, 2.0, 6.0), 3.0, 1e-12); CHECK_NEAR(mean_of(1, 2.5), 2.5, 1e-12); CHECK_NEAR(mean_of(0), 0.0, 1e-12); float f = 0.5f; CHECK_NEAR(mean_of(2, f, 1.5), 1.0, 1e-12); }
